decisions.reason: Define-XML ADADAS.CHG states AVAL - BASE on every record, but adadas.r L164-L168 runs derive_var_chg only where ABLFL is missing, and ABLFL is QS.QSBLFL, so baseline records keep a missing CHG instead of zero. The rest of the program (L156-L173) adds no other CHG step.

Define-XML ADADAS.CHG states only AVAL - BASE, its literal probe gives 0 on the 3800 records where the reference leaves CHG missing, and ADRG pages 17, 45 and 48 add no baseline condition. The CHG__NONBASELINE reading is labelled as the adadas.r lines 164-168 computation (derive_var_chg restricted to is.na(ABLFL)), which explains how the reference was computed without being treated as documentation.

Define-XML ADADAS.PCHG states 100* (CHG/BASE) on every record, but adadas.r L169-L173 runs derive_var_pchg only where ABLFL is missing, so baseline records keep a missing PCHG. No other program line sets PCHG.

ADRG page 11's placement of visits by date and window corresponds to the obs AVISIT windowing (adadas_v1.yaml lines 438-446), not to the visit of an added record. ADRG page 47's R-generated example shows the Week 16 LOCF record carrying the Week 8 record's VISIT, ADT and ADY, as locf8, locf16 and locf24 do.

CL.AVISITN is shared by IT.ADADAS.AVISITN and IT.ADLBC.AVISITN (native define-adam.xml lines 1190 and 1579), so its other entries serve ADLBC's visits. The obs mapping (adadas_v1.yaml lines 456-459) gives the codelist's own codes for Baseline, Week 8, Week 16 and Week 24, the only AVISIT values the specification derives.

Each LOCF template takes ADT and ADY from the same donor record (locf8, adadas_v1.yaml lines 537-538 and 548-549), whose ADY obs computed by study_day from that ADT and TRTSDT, so the copy equals the Define-XML ADADAS.ADY formula on the record's own ADT. ADRG page 47 shows the same for the added Week 16 record (ADT 2013-05-22, ADY 60 from the Week 8 record).

Define-XML ADADAS.BASE adds (QS.VISITNUM=3) to QS.QSBLFL=Y, while the BASE aggregate (adadas_v1.yaml lines 391-401) filters only ABLFL = 'Y' and no layer conditions on VISITNUM. Every ADAS-Cog QSBLFL=Y record in the staged QS is at VISITNUM 3, so the values agree and this is a divergence rather than a conflict.

Define-XML ADADAS.AVISIT delegates windowing to SAP Section 8.2, which is not among Pilot 3's section files and whose applicability is pending_review in spec/source/manifest.json, and ADRG page 11 says only that visits are windowed by date. No retained document gives the study-day cut points or the otherwise branch to Week 24 (adadas_v1.yaml lines 438-446); adadas.r lines 70-75 show the reference's windows, not documentation.

Define-XML ADADAS.DTYPE only labels imputed ACTOT records LOCF, and ADRG pages 45-47 give the number of imputed records and one added Week 16 record. No retained document states the locf8 condition (repeated in locf16 and locf24) for adding a record; adadas.r lines 118-142 show how the reference added them, not documentation.

ADRG page 11 states that ADADAS holds the ADAS-Cog questionnaire items, one record per subject per parameter per VISIT, and Define-XML ADADAS.PARAMCD limits the parameters to the CL.PARAMCD_ADQSADAS codes ACITM01-ACITM14 and ACTOT, with QS.QSTESTCD as predecessor (native define-adam.xml line 1248). Together they state this QS record selection (adadas_v1.yaml line 425).

The windows in adadas.r lines 67-76 and 118-142 show how the reference was computed and cannot supply the documented rule.

No retained text states the general restriction to ANL01FL = 'Y' ACTOT donors at or before the target visit that adadas_v2.yaml lines 71-72 apply.

Define-XML CL.DTYPE's 'Last Observation Carried Forward' gives only the direction of the carry, and ADRG page 47 illustrates one carried record. No retained document states the DONOR8 ranking by AVISITN, then ADY, then QSSEQ, all descending with missing values last (adadas_v1.yaml lines 102-112).

Define-XML ADADAS.ADT states only 'SAS date from QS.QSDTC', and the day-01 imputation in ADRG page 8 section 3.4 is stated for ADAE ASTDT, not ADADAS ADT. No retained document states imputing a missing QSDTC day as the first of the month (adadas_v1.yaml lines 432-433).

Define-XML ADADAS.CHG states only AVAL - BASE, and ADRG pages 17 and 45-48 add no condition on baseline records, so the guard ABLFL <> 'Y' (adadas_v1.yaml line 407) is unstated. adadas.r lines 164-168 restrict the reference's subtraction to records without ABLFL, which explains the reference but is not documentation.

Define-XML ADADAS.PCHG and workbook Methods row 12 state only 100* (CHG/BASE), and no ADRG page adds a baseline-record or zero-baseline condition. The guard ABLFL <> 'Y' AND BASE <> 0 (adadas_v1.yaml line 414) is therefore unstated.

Define-XML ADADAS.PCHG states 100* (CHG/BASE) without saying what PCHG is when BASE is 0, and the ADRG supplies no such policy, so the literal expression is undefined on zero-baseline records and cannot be stated as a probe. adadas.r lines 169-173 leave that case to admiral's derive_var_pchg, which is computation, not documentation.

Define-XML ADADAS.ANL01FL chooses the visit closest to the target date but gives no rule for two equally close visits, and the ADRG page 46-47 example has no such tie. The second sort key _DIFF (adadas_v1.yaml lines 483-484) is therefore unstated; adadas.r lines 106 and 111 use the same key for the reference, which is not documentation.

Define-XML ADADAS.ANL01FL ranks by closeness to the target date and does not say how a record without a distance is ranked. Placing missing AWTDIFF last (adadas_v1.yaml lines 481-482) has no counterpart in the retained documents.

Define-XML ADADAS.ANL01FL selects among the visits that fall into the same visit window, with no condition on the score, and ADRG page 11 gives one record per subject per parameter per VISIT, so ranking every collected record of a subject, parameter and AVISIT states that rule. Added LOCF records never compete, since locf8, locf16 and locf24 add one only where the visit has no flagged ACTOT record, and ADRG page 47 shows such a record flagged Y.

Define-XML ADADAS.ANL01FL gives nearest-to-target selection but no tie rule, and the target day is delegated by ADADAS.AWTARGET to the SAP, which is not among Pilot 3's section files and whose applicability is pending_review in spec/source/manifest.json; ADRG pages 46-47 illustrate one subject's flags without completing those choices. adadas.r lines 104-116 and 143-144 show how the reference set the flag, which cannot supply the documented rule.

The expected-visit table in adadas.r lines 118-142 shows how the reference added records, not documentation, so an independent probe would still have to borrow the specification or the reference DTYPE.
